subject: fluid_mechanics
title: Friction Losses in Fluid Flow in Pipes
aim: To determine the Frictional Head Loss (hf), Flow Velocity (v), Reynolds Number (NRe), and Friction Factor (f) for fluid flow through pipes.
apparatus: Collecting tank (0.4 m × 0.4 m) with water level indicator and stopwatch
theory:
The liquid flowing under pressure in a pipeline is subjected to head loss due to friction. Frictional resistance causes a loss of pressure head along the direction of flow.

Differential Manometer Reading:
\Delta h = \frac{|h_1 - h_2|}{100} \quad (\text{m})

Head Loss due to Friction:
h_f = \Delta h \times 12.6 \quad (\text{m})

Volumetric Flow Rate:
Q = \frac{\text{Volume}}{\text{Time}} = \frac{A_{tank} \times rise}{t} = \frac{0.4 \times 0.4 \times 0.1}{t} = \frac{0.016}{t} \quad (\text{m}^3/\text{s})

Flow Velocity:
v = \frac{Q}{A} = \frac{Q}{\frac{\pi D^2}{4}} = \frac{Q}{1.2265 \times 10^{-4}} \quad (\text{m/s})

Reynolds Number:
N_{Re} = \frac{D \cdot v \cdot \rho}{\mu} = \frac{0.0125 \times v \times 1000}{0.001}

Friction Factor (Blasius Equation):
f = \frac{0.079}{(N_{Re})^{1/4}}
procedure: Fill the sump tank with water and open the inlet valve.
Start the centrifugal pump and allow water to flow through the pipe test section.
Purge air bubbles from the manometer connecting tubes.
Adjust the outlet control valve to achieve the desired flow rate.
Record manometer limb readings h1 and h2 (in cm).
Measure the time t (in seconds) taken for 10 cm (0.1 m) water level rise in the collecting tank.
Repeat the experiment for 5 different flow rates and calculate Δh, hf, Q, v, NRe, and f.

formulas.label: Differential Manometer Level (Δh)
formulas.derivation:
Manometer head difference converted from cm to meters:

\Delta h = \frac{|h_1 - h_2|}{100} \text{ (m)}
formulas.purpose: Converts differential limb reading to meters.

formulas.label: Head Loss due to Friction (hf)
formulas.derivation:
Equivalent water head loss derived from mercury manometer differential reading:

h_f = \Delta h \times (S_{Hg} - S_w) = \Delta h \times 12.6 \text{ (m)}
formulas.purpose: Calculates frictional head loss in meters of water.
assumptions: Mercury specific gravity = 13.6, Water specific gravity = 1.0
formulas.practical_application: Quantifies energy head loss due to pipe friction.

formulas.label: Volumetric Flow Rate (Q)
formulas.derivation:
Flow rate computed from collecting tank dimensions (0.4m × 0.4m × 0.1m = 0.016 m³):

Q = \frac{0.016}{t} \text{ (m³/s)}

formulas.label: Flow Velocity (v)
assumptions: Uniform velocity profile across pipe section
formulas.practical_application: Determines fluid momentum and Reynolds number.

formulas.label: Reynolds Number (NRe)
formulas.derivation:
Dimensionless ratio of inertial to viscous forces:

N_{Re} = \frac{0.0125 \times v \times 1000}{0.001}

formulas.label: Friction Factor (f)
formulas.derivation:
Blasius correlation for smooth pipe turbulent flow:

f = \frac{0.079}{(N_{Re})^{0.25}}
formulas.practical_application: Predicts head loss in hydraulic networks.

precautions: Operate the control valves gently to prevent pressure surges.
Ensure all air bubbles are thoroughly purged from manometer tubes before taking readings.
Maintain steady water flow while timing the water rise in the measuring tank.
